articles.title: Punjab polls: Badal praises SAD-BJP rule as Amit Shah’s NDA pitch fuels reunion buzz
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Speculation over a possible reunion between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) gathered pace on Friday after
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Speculation over a possible reunion between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) gathered pace on Friday after SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal said his party was open to an alliance with parties that agree with its ideology and programmes, a day after Union home minister Amit Shah predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027.Badal, however, ruled out any understanding with the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling them the “two biggest enemies of Punjab”."During the SAD-BJP rule, peace prevailed in Punjab, and the state witnessed development, be it in infrastructure, industry, or the state becoming power surplus," Badal told reporters on Friday, according to PTI."Whether we form the government or not, we will continue to fight for the people of Punjab. In our view, the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party are the two biggest enemies of Punjab, and we can never have understanding with these parties. There are many other parties besides these and those who agree with the Akali Dal's ideology and programmes; we are open (for a tie-up)," he said.The remarks came a day after Union minister Amit Shah said Punjab's people had decided that an NDA government would come to power in the state in the 2027 assembly elections. He also predicted that the ruling AAP would be wiped out in the polls.Shah's statement reignited speculation about the BJP and SAD joining hands again, although Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon denied that any alliance decision had been taken."We have nothing on an alliance as of now. We are prepared for all 117 seats and will contest on all of them," Dhillon told TOI, adding that the BJP referred to its government at the Centre as an NDA government and would do the same in Punjab.A senior Punjab BJP functionary, however, said the political signal was clear despite Shah not naming the Akali Dal. The functionary also felt the two parties should have announced an alliance earlier, given the limited time before the elections. Any formal announcement would have to come from BJP national president Nitin Nabin, the functionary said.Why a SAD-BJP reunion mattersThe SAD and BJP were long-time allies in Punjab before the regional party ended their 24-year-old alliance in September 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws. SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Sukhbir Singh Badal's wife, had also served as a Cabinet minister in the Narendra Modi government before the split.The former allies contested elections together for years, but their political fortunes were limited in the 2022 Punjab assembly polls. The BJP won two seats, while the SAD secured three in the 117-member Assembly.In recent months, several Punjab BJP leaders had maintained that the party was preparing to contest all 117 assembly seats independently. Dhillon reiterated that position on Friday, even as Shah's remarks and Badal's openness to an alliance renewed questions about the parties' electoral plans.Badal made the comments after leading an SAD delegation to meet Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday. The delegation submitted a memorandum over the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and demanded, among other measures, the dismissal of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.Badal accused the AAP government of mishandling Punjab's affairs and said the state's law and order situation had deteriorated. He also blamed the Congress and AAP governments for what he described as the worsening situation in the state.With the 2027 assembly elections approaching, the public statements have revived the possibility of a realignment between the former allies. However, neither party has announced a formal agreement, and the BJP's Punjab leadership continues to maintain that it is preparing to contest all 117 seats.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US draws up $78bn-plan for 850 F-35 jets; eyes Air Force fleet of 1,509 fighters by 2035
articles.summary: The Pentagon has struck a 10-year framework with Lockheed Martin for at least 850 F-35 stealth fighters, in a deal aimed at expanding production,
articles.body: The Pentagon has struck a 10-year framework with Lockheed Martin for at least 850 F-35 stealth fighters, in a deal aimed at expanding production, strengthening the supply chain and addressing persistent aircraft readiness problems.According to Defense News, the agreement, announced on October 22, remains subject to congressional approval and funding. It also includes spare parts, modification kits and sustainment support, while Lockheed Martin has pledged at least $7 billion in company-funded investments to support the programme.The framework targets an average of 85 aircraft annually for US forces over the next decade, in line with the Pentagon's fiscal 2027 procurement request. The planned production rate of 156 aircraft a year, meanwhile, includes orders for international customers, reflecting the F-35 programme's global scale.Reuters estimated the 10-year framework to be worth at least $78.2 billion, based on the F-35A's $92 million unit price, the cheapest of the three variants. The US Marine Corps' F-35B costs about $121 million per aircraft, while the US Navy's F-35C is priced at approximately $110 million.The final value will depend on the mix of variants, with prices also expected to rise due to inflation and labour costs, Reuters reported.The agreement comes as the US military struggles to keep its existing F-35 fleet operational. A Government Accountability Office report published in June found that the aircraft's mission-capable rate fell from 67 percent in fiscal 2021 to 44 percent in fiscal 2025.The proportion of time the jets could perform all their assigned missions declined from 38 percent to 25 percent over the same period.Lockheed Martin expects predictable orders for spare parts and maintenance support to help reduce repair delays and improve aircraft availability.US Air Force plans 1,509-fighter fleet by 2035The US Air Force aims to build a fleet of 1,509 combat-coded fighter aircraft by 2035, with the F-35A expected to become its largest fighter component as the service modernises its combat aviation capabilities.According to Defense News, the target was outlined in a force structure report submitted to Congress on October 16, 2026. The plan envisages the F-35A accounting for around 40 percent of the fleet, while the F-22 Raptor and its planned successor, the F-47, would together make up approximately 20 percent. F-15 and F-16 variants would account for the remaining 40 percent.The service also plans to field 500 Collaborative Combat Aircraft, or autonomous drone wingmen, by 2032. These aircraft are not included in the 1,509-fighter target, although officials expect future advances in autonomous systems could change the number of crewed fighters required.

articles.title: 'Won't tolerate vote theft': Anti-SIR protesters try to march to EC HQ, many detained
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police detained several protesters on Friday as a march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls headed towards
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police detained several protesters on Friday as a march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls headed towards the Election Commission (EC) headquarters in central Delhi. Authorities imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), banning mass gatherings, sources said.The demonstration was called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, a people's collective, and drew students, youth, farmers and activists carrying the national flag and banners of the group.The Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) and the Students' Federation of India (SFI) also extended their support, with activists from Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh joining the march.Amid slogans such as “Gyanesh Kumar, resign”, “Halt SIR” and “Won’t tolerate vote theft”, the protesters were joined by senior CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and members of the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA) and the All India Democratic Students' Organisation (AIDSO), among others.The march began near Gole Dak Khana, at the intersection of Kalibari Marg and Bhai Vir Singh Marg, and proceeded towards the ECI headquarters. When police stopped the protesters, they sat down and held a 'People's Parliament', as announced by the organisers.“The protest has begun! We won't let go our right to vote and the right to protest for it! Our's is a democratic country and we will ensure that spirit remains alive!” the All India Students' Association (AISA) said in a post on X.“This is not about reclaiming Jantar Mantar; this is about saving democracy and the country,” a protester said, as cited by PTI.Another protester said that since Jantar Mantar had been denotified as a protest site, every street in the country would become a Jantar Mantar, pointing to several organisations announcing demonstrations across India.Protests planned across 88 citiesPeople Against SIR has launched a website providing information about demonstrations being held in different cities. According to the collective, protests have been planned in 88 cities across 18 states, involving 145 organisations.The collective has listed demonstrations scheduled for Friday, with programmes extending until November 1 as part of its campaign against the SIR exercise. Organisers have appealed to farmers, workers, youth, women and people from different sections of society to participate while carrying the national flag.The organisers said the Delhi march would remain peaceful and conclude with the adoption of resolutions and the singing of the national anthem. The SFI has also called for solidarity protests in central Delhi and at district headquarters on Friday.Security tightened, traffic diversions in placeSecurity was tightened in central Delhi, with Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed in large numbers.Traffic diversions were enforced in parts of central Delhi from 1 pm and were scheduled to remain in place until 5 pm. Congestion was expected around Bangla Sahib Gurudwara, Connaught Place, Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar.The Delhi Traffic Police advised commuters to avoid unnecessary travel along the affected stretches, plan their journeys and follow instructions issued by traffic personnel.The protest comes amid concerns raised by opposition parties and various organisations over the SIR exercise and the alleged deletion of voters from electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: The backstory: How a battle in Egypt's desert turned the tide of World War II
articles.summary: “This is not the end. It is not even the beginning of the end.
articles.body: “This is not the end. It is not even the beginning of the end. But it is perhaps the end of the beginning.”- Winston Churchill, November 10, 1942, following the Allied victory in the Second Battle of El Alamein.Eight decades ago, as World War II raged, Nazi Germany had overrun France and pushed deep into the Soviet Union, while Japan captured Singapore in February 1942 in one of Britain's worst military defeats. In June, German General Erwin Rommel's forces captured the Libyan port of Tobruk, pushing Allied troops towards Egypt and bringing the Suez Canal within reach.Thus, it appeared that the Axis powers had the upper hand until a massive artillery barrage broke the quiet of Egypt's western desert, triggering a 13-day battle that ultimately marked a change in the course of the war.The second battle of El Alamein began on October 23, 1942 between the Allied forces led by the British and the Axis powers of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy. By November 4, the Allies had gotten one of their most important victories.The question here is: why did a battle fought in a desert stretch near a small railway station in North Africa matter so much?Why North Africa was so importantNorth Africa became a key battleground in World War II because of Egypt's strategic location and the Suez Canal, a vital shipping route connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and linking Britain to its territories in Asia. Control of Egypt also threatened Britain's access to Middle Eastern oil supplies.The campaign began in 1940, when Italy, advancing from its North African colony of Libya, invaded Egypt but was pushed back by British and Commonwealth forces later that year. Germany intervened in 1941 to support its Italian ally, sending troops under General Erwin Rommel, nicknamed the "Desert Fox".Rommel had won several battles and pushed British forces back towards Egypt. His forces moved into Egypt after taking Tobruk in June 1942, but they were stopped in July at the First Battle of El Alamein. Although that battle ended in stalemate, the Allies had managed to halt the Axis' advance on Alexandria and the Suez Canal.The location played a crucial role in stopping the Axis advance. German and Italian tanks found it difficult to get around British defensive positions due to the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the mostly impassable Qattara Depression to the south. This geographical advantage aided the British to hold their ground, setting the stage for a decisive fight three months later.What happened on October 23, 1942By October, British commander Bernard Montgomery had assembled more than 190,000 Allied troops and over 1,000 tanks. Standing against them were approximately 116,000 German and Italian soldiers with around 540 tanks.The British-led Eighth Army was a multinational force, including troops from India, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.Rommel, meanwhile, faced a serious problem. His army was running short of fuel, ammunition and supplies as Allied aircraft, warships and submarines disrupted shipments across the Mediterranean.The fighting was fierce however. Allied tanks struggled to cross the minefields and suffered heavy losses from German anti-tank guns. The initial assault failed to achieve the breakthrough Montgomery had hoped for, as it turned into a struggle to wear down Axis defences.Then, Montgomery changed tactics, ordering Australian troops to intensify their attacks in the north, near the Mediterranean coast. This drew German forces towards that sector, weakening their positions further south. On November 2, New Zealand and British troops launched Operation Supercharge against the weakened defences. At those moments, Allied forces broke through, and by November 4, Rommel's army was retreating.Turning of the tideThe El Alamein battle ended the Axis threat to Egypt and the Suez Canal and gave Britain a victory after years of military setbacks.Then, just four days later, on November 8, American and British forces landed in Morocco and Algeria as part of Operation Torch, establishing a new front against Axis forces in North Africa. Due to their position between Allied advances from the east and west, German and Italian forces were ultimately defeated. The Allied invasion of Sicily in July 1943 was made possible by the surrender of the remaining Axis forces in Tunisia by May 1943.Thus, the second battle of El Alamein was a significant turning point in World War II. The victory weakened Axis dominance of the Mediterranean, secured a vital strategic area, and made way for later Allied campaigns in Europe.Eighty-four years later, the battle serves as a reminder that the fight for victory in World War II went well beyond the boundaries of Europe and into the North African deserts.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel heads to US after Trump’s surprise deal with Moscow
articles.summary: A tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is headed for New York, according to ship-tracking data released on Friday, following a deal
articles.body: A tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is headed for New York, according to ship-tracking data released on Friday, following a deal reached between Moscow and Washington earlier this month.The Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low-sulphur diesel at Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, Reuters reported, citing LSEG shipping data. The vessel is expected to arrive in the United States on November 7.Also Read | Trump’s Russian roulette: A high-stakes juggle between Vladimir Putin and the pollsThe identities of the buyer and seller were not immediately known. The shipment would mark the first US import of Russian oil or petroleum products since then-President Joe Biden announced a ban on such imports in 2022.The development comes after US President Donald Trump announced the surprise deal on October 9 as part of efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections. The agreement also involved Russia lifting a self-imposed ban on diesel exports.Trump also waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Moscow and threatened to ban diesel exports to Europe unless countries released more fuel from their emergency reserves to help ease prices.Further shipments to follow?As announced by Trump on October 9, Russia was to "immediately export" 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November and another 1 million tons "immediately thereafter".Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak indicated that further shipments would follow as Russian and US companies finalise delivery contracts. He also projected that Russia could raise its diesel exports to their usual levels of 3 million to 3.5 million tons per month by the end of the year.Last week, Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who also heads Russia’s sovereign wealth fund, revealed that the US Treasury had approached the fund for assistance in resolving complex payment issues related to the agreement.Since the European Union imposed a full embargo on imports of Russian oil products in February 2023 over the war in Ukraine, which began in February 2022, Russia has primarily exported diesel to Brazil and Turkey, as well as to countries across Africa.You use AI every day. articles.title: Indian-origin woman among immigrants charged in US voter fraud crackdown; citizenship bid at risk
articles.summary: An Indian-origin woman is among more than two dozen legal permanent residents charged by federal authorities in California as part of a crackdown on
articles.body: An Indian-origin woman is among more than two dozen legal permanent residents charged by federal authorities in California as part of a crackdown on alleged noncitizen voter registration and voting ahead of the US midterm elections. The charges could jeopardise their efforts to become American citizens, with some facing years in prison and potential deportation.According to the Associated Press, Amandeep Kaur, who has lived in the US for eight years and is in the process of becoming a US citizen, is among those charged.Her husband, Kulwinder Singh, said she obtained her driver’s licence in 2024 and may have registered to vote while applying for it. Singh said his wife took the written driving test in Hindi because she struggles with English.Singh said his wife received and returned a ballot in 2024, but both believed it was a voter registration form. He said Kaur was now distraught over the possibility that she had unknowingly broken the law.“All she does is cry. It’s heartbreaking,” Singh, who is a US citizen, told The Associated Press (AP).Federal authorities charged more than two dozen legal permanent residents in California on Monday over allegations of illegally registering to vote or voting as noncitizens. By Thursday morning, prosecutors had filed charging documents in 10 of the 28 cases, providing details of how investigators used voter registration records to pursue criminal charges involving immigration status.Citizenship applications at centre of several casesMost of the immigrants charged had applied for US citizenship and now face allegations of lying on naturalisation applications or during immigration interviews. Such charges could complicate or derail their attempts to become citizens.One of the accused, José Antonio Bañuelos-Díaz, 42, applied for citizenship in October 2025 after living in the US for 40 years as a legal permanent resident. The government alleges he improperly claimed to be a US citizen when registering to vote in 2007 and later failed to disclose it on immigration paperwork. Authorities have not accused him of casting a ballot.Bañuelos-Díaz told AP he did not know he had registered to vote until he was arrested outside his Los Angeles home on Monday. He recalled obtaining a driver’s licence around 2007. In California, people are prompted to register to vote when applying for a driving licence.He was released after his arrest but faces up to five years in prison if convicted.Trump administration steps up scrutiny ahead of midtermsThe cases form part of the Trump administration’s broader campaign against alleged noncitizen voting before the November midterm elections, despite data showing that such voting is rare and has not been demonstrated to change election outcomes.The Justice Department said six people would be charged with voting as noncitizens, a misdemeanour. The remaining 22 face a combination of felony charges, including allegedly lying on naturalisation applications, during interviews or on voter registration forms.Noncitizens convicted of illegally voting face up to one year in prison, while those convicted of lying on applications for US citizenship can face up to 10 years.The Justice Department has also sued California over its refusal to verify the citizenship status of roughly 20,000 registered voters whom the federal government suspects may be noncitizens. California, which has more than 23 million registered voters, has maintained that it complies with federal law and argued that the administration's figures are likely significantly inflated.State election officials have also pointed out that once ballots are mailed in, they are separated from individual voter identification, making it impossible to isolate ballots based on the information supplied by federal authorities.The Department of Homeland Security did not explain what initially brought the accused immigrants to investigators' attention. However, it said the agency reviewed naturalisation and other records as part of its investigation. Some court documents refer to a benefits fraud audit conducted by Homeland Security in August that may have helped identify those charged.“The voting rights of American citizens must be protected,” First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement announcing the charges.Naturalisation approvals decline sharplyThe crackdown comes amid wider immigration enforcement under President Donald Trump and a slowdown in the processing of citizenship applications.Government data showed that officials approved 58,000 naturalisation applications between April and June 2026, less than a quarter of the number approved during the same period in 2025.Green card holders can generally apply for US citizenship after three years if they meet the requirements applicable to spouses of US citizens, or after five years under the standard eligibility route.Applicants must undergo background checks, answer detailed questions about voting, political activities and criminal history, pass a civics test and meet English language requirements.For immigrants already seeking citizenship, allegations involving voter registration or voting can have consequences extending beyond the immediate criminal proceedings, potentially affecting their naturalisation applications and immigration status.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, Leonardo DiCaprio's conservation group helped buy more than 52,000 acres on a Chilean island to prevent mining and logging; a year later, its future as a protected area is being negotiated
articles.summary: More than a year after a conservation group linked to Leonardo DiCaprio helped acquire over 52,000 acres on Chile’s Guafo Island, efforts are continuing
articles.body: More than a year after a conservation group linked to Leonardo DiCaprio helped acquire over 52,000 acres on Chile’s Guafo Island, efforts are continuing to secure its future as a protected area. The purchase, completed in 2025 for US$7.5 million, was intended to prevent destructive development and preserve the island’s wildlife and forests. According to Chilean newspaper La Tercera, which reported on the organisation’s financial records and negotiations on October 17, 2026, Re:wild (Re), the conservation organisation linked to DiCaprio, and its local partners are working with Chilean authorities on a legal framework for protection. The process also involves Indigenous communities with longstanding cultural and traditional ties to the island.How the island was acquired for conservationGuafo Island lies off the coast of Chiloé, in southern Chile, near the municipality of Quellón. It covers an ecologically important landscape that has attracted interest from coal mining and timber harvesting industries. In June 2025, Re announced that it had joined the Jeff and Marieke Rothschild Foundation, the Wyss Foundation and Art into Acres in purchasing the majority of the island from a private owner. WWF Chile and Corporación Cultiva later joined the follow-up conservation work.According to Re, the acquisition secured approximately 21,000 hectares, or 52,000 acres, against the threat of extractive development. The organisation said it intended to donate the property to the Chilean state so it could become a national park. The purchase was significant because much of the island’s coastal forest remains undisturbed. Re said the forest had never been logged and that non-native livestock had not grazed there, helping preserve its natural ecosystems.However, purchasing the land was only the first step. Its long-term protection requires an appropriate legal designation, consultation with stakeholders and arrangements for future management.Why Guafo Island matters for wildlifeGuafo Island is recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area, a designation identifying places important for the persistence of biodiversity. Re has highlighted the island’s importance for seabirds, including the world’s largest breeding colony of near-threatened sooty shearwaters and a breeding colony of Magellanic penguins. The island also supports southern fur seals and endangered marine otters.Its surrounding waters form part of a productive marine ecosystem frequented by whales, including endangered blue and sei whales. Protecting the island therefore has implications beyond its forests and terrestrial wildlife, extending to the wider coastal environment. Conservationists argue that preventing mining and logging could help maintain these interconnected habitats. Yet formal protection must also account for the people who depend on the island’s marine resources and regard it as part of their cultural heritage.Negotiations with Chilean authoritiesAccording to La Tercera, Re’s local partner, Corporación Cultiva, began working with Chile’s Biodiversity and Protected Areas Service, known as SBAP, in February 2026 to advance the protection process. The proposed route includes establishing a private protected area before potentially transferring the property to the state. Re told the newspaper that its technical dossier was nearing completion and was expected to be submitted to the regional authorities in Los Lagos in the coming weeks.The dossier is intended to document the island’s environmental importance and support its proposed legal designation. The process will involve assessment and review, including responses to any requests for additional information. Re indicated that the process could conclude in November 2027, although the timeline may change depending on administrative requirements and Chile’s evolving biodiversity legislation.However, the acquisition has not yet resulted in full operational protection. According to La Tercera, permanent staff and park rangers had not been established on the island, and management and surveillance measures were still pending. Indigenous participation is another important consideration. Mapuche-Williche communities have sought recognition of a coastal marine area for Indigenous peoples, known as an ECMPO, covering waters and resources they traditionally use. Re has expressed support for that application and said it is maintaining dialogue with community representatives.What Re:wild’s financial records revealThe island purchase also features prominently in Re’s finances. La Tercera reported that the organisation recorded consolidated assets of approximately US$74 million and net assets of US$61 million at the end of June 2025. The US$7.5 million landholding was listed as its sole property asset. articles.title: US DoJ probing DHS contracting kickbacks involving Trump ally Corey Lewandowski; President says 'dishonest officials should be prosecuted'
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice is probing kickback allegations involving Corey Lewandowski, a Trump ally, linked to contracts at the Department of Homeland Security, amid accusations of bias in investigation practices.
articles.body: US Department of Justice prosecutors are examining allegations of possible kickbacks linked to contracting at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with investigators awaiting findings from an internal watchdog probe, according to people familiar with the matter.The investigation involves Corey Lewandowski, a longtime ally of President Donald Trump who served as a senior adviser to former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.The referral comes amid questions about the Trump administration's handling of allegations involving its own officials. Critics have accused the Justice Department of pursuing the president's political opponents while failing to subject administration allies to similar scrutiny.According to a source familiar with the investigation cited by the outlet, Washington, DC, US Attorney Jeanine Pirro had told officials in her office in recent months that she wanted investigators to examine claims of kickbacks connected to DHS contracts. It remains unclear which US Attorney's office is leading the investigation.Prosecutors have been waiting for the results of an inquiry by the DHS inspector general, another person familiar with the matter said.Lewandowski became a prominent figure at DHS during Trump's second term, serving as Noem's chief adviser. He was initially appointed as a special government employee, a designation intended for people serving the government for a limited number of days.His involvement in senior department functions while holding that status was unusual. Officials came to view him as a key gatekeeper for Noem, who left the department after Trump dismissed her.Noem's management of DHS contracts was among the issues that contributed to her departure earlier this year. One point of controversy involved a $220 million advertising campaign that prominently featured Noem. She said Trump knew about the campaign.During her tenure, Noem also required contracts and grants worth more than $100,000 to receive her approval. She defended the policy as a way to reduce waste, although several DHS officials considered the requirement unnecessary.The department's inspector general, Joseph Cuffari, told Congress in early March that senior DHS officials had obstructed some of his work.Trump addressed the investigation into Lewandowski on Thursday, telling reporters he had only recently learned about it. He said he wanted any officials found to be dishonest to face prosecution.“They’re stealing from me, so I want my people to be honest,” Trump said. “And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do.”You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Head of customs brother of CEC Gyanesh Kumar': Bhagwant Mann on 'detention' at Delhi airport
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has alleged that he was kept waiting for around two hours at Delhi airport after returning from Paris,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has alleged that he was kept waiting for around two hours at Delhi airport after returning from Paris, claiming that officials repeatedly cited luggage checks as the reason for the delay. Mann also alleged that the head of ustoms at the airport, identified as Manish, is the brother of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“They kept us seated there for two hours, repeatedly saying that they were checking our luggage. But they found nothing in our luggage. The head of customs at Delhi Airport, Manish, is the real brother of Gyanesh Kumar,” Mann said.The allegation comes after the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) claimed that Mann was detained for three hours at the airport late on Monday and issued a challan of Rs 50,000 upon his return from a food trade fair in Paris.AAP state media in-charge Baltej Pannu alleged that the incident was part of a deliberate attempt by the BJP-led Centre to humiliate Mann and undermine Punjab's dignity. He claimed that officials initially told the chief minister that his luggage was still arriving or being checked.According to Pannu, Mann was allowed to leave after several hours but was issued the challan when he was about to depart in his vehicle. Pannu alleged that officials told Mann they were under “tremendous pressure from above”. He did not specify the reason for the challan.Shiromani Akali Dal general secretary Bikram Singh Majithia also posted on X that Mann and his wife were questioned for hours over allegations that they were carrying more luggage or money than permitted. Majithia claimed that officials subsequently ordered checks of the bags belonging to the entire chief minister's office staff.The controversy follows a dispute between the Punjab government and the Centre over Mann's Paris visit. After the Centre denied him political clearance, the Punjab government approached the Punjab and Haryana high court, which set aside the decision, observing that the Centre “had not explained what that political angle/viewpoint is”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday criticised the Centre after a Delhi court allowed American mercenary Matthew Aaron VanDyke to
articles.body: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday criticised the Centre after a Delhi court allowed American mercenary Matthew Aaron VanDyke to travel to the United States.He linked the decision to the deployment of security forces in Delhi to prevent protests, alleging that forces had been moved away from border areas amid tensions with China."There are two big news update from today Mathew Vandyke the American mercenary who was training terrorists in Myanmar was allowed to go to US by the court. And why wouldn't he be we was "just" training terrorists and not waving the Tiranga. Another update is that our forces have said that it is tough to fight China. And why wouldn't it be when the Modi government has taken forces out of border areas and deployed them in Delhi so that no one can protest in Delhi," Dipke said in a video posted on X.A Delhi court on Friday allowed VanDyke to travel to the United States and extended permission for six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24.Special Judge Prashant Sharma passed the order while hearing applications filed by the seven foreign nationals.VanDyke and the six Ukrainians were arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March 2026 for allegedly providing weapons and drone-warfare training to ethnic armed groups in Myanmar.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das appeared before a Special Executive Magistrate on Friday for verification of their sureties following their release from judicial custody.After appearing before the magistrate, Ranka said the movement would continue regardless of whether the party's leaders were in jail or outside."There was a verification process for our sureties. Everything went well, and we have been given a new date sometime in the third week of November," Ranka said.“The movement will continue. We are not leaders; we are custodians of this platform that the people of this country have given us, and we are just trying to do our best. The movement will continue whether we are in jail or outside. We have learnt a lot about ourselves and how the regime operates. We will, of course, change and evolve as necessary,” he added.Ranka and Das were released from judicial custody after the Special Executive Magistrate's court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.In their undertakings, the two leaders pledged not to breach the peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.“Further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage, particularly after written undertakings before this Court,” the court observed while ordering their release.Ranka and Das were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. Police alleged that the two entered the area through private premises and violated conditions imposed to maintain peace.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ankita Bhandari murder case: Actress Urmila Sanawar agrees to CBI’s proposed narco test amid 'VIP' audio clips row
articles.summary: DEHRADUN/HARIDWAR: CBI served a notice on actress Urmila Sanawar regarding a possible narcoanalysis test in connection with the 2022 Rishikesh resort
articles.body: DEHRADUN/HARIDWAR: CBI served a notice on actress Urmila Sanawar regarding a possible narcoanalysis test in connection with the 2022 Rishikesh resort murder case.Sanawar had released audio recordings allegedly linking senior BJP leader Dushyant Gautam to the ‘VIP’ controversy surrounding the killing.The actress said on Wednesday that she was willing to undergo the test and cooperate with investigators, claiming it could help establish the truth and identify others allegedly connected with the case.The development followed CBI’s recent questioning of expelled BJP leader and former MLA Suresh Rathore, whose alleged conversations with Sanawar had surfaced in the recordings.Sanawar, who had earlier released several audio clips purportedly involving Rathore, claimed the recordings contained references to Gautam as the alleged ‘VIP’ in the case.The allegations made in the recordings remain unsubstantiated, and investigators had not announced any findings linking Gautam to the murder. Gautam has also vehemently denied the allegations.Speaking to TOI on Thursday, Sanawar said, “A notice regarding the narco test was served by the CBI and I am happy about that. Though I am suffering from fever, I will reach Dehradun on Friday.”She also posted a video on social media expressing her willingness to undergo the procedure, even suggesting that it be conducted live.During an earlier police inquiry, investigators had seized Sanawar’s mobile phone and sent the disputed audio recordings for forensic examination along with voice samples of Rathore and Sanawar.Meanwhile, the victim’s parents said they were awaiting further developments in the probe, particularly the proposed narcoanalysis tests.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: JNAC plans digitisation of birth, death certificates issued since 1945
articles.summary: JNAC plans to digitise 10.5 lakh birth and death certificates issued from 1945–2015 to preserve ageing records and speed retrieval; state approval awaited.
articles.body: Jamshedpur: Birth and death certificates, issued between 1945 and 2015, will now be digitised by Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee (JNAC). The move, officials said, is aimed at preserving ageing paper documents and cutting the time and effort needed to trace old certificates. It could also help residents obtain information about their own certificates or those of family members.JNAC municipal commissioner Yogendra Prasad said the civic body is still in its planning stages, and the process could take time because many old paper certificates were in poor condition. JNAC would need clearance from the state urban development and housing department for implementing the project.JNAC officials estimate that over 10.5 lakh birth and death certificates were issued in the 70 years. On average, 15,000 birth and death certificates are issued annually.“Paper records were being preserved to prevent damage, deterioration or loss over time. Paper documents can become damaged, torn or illegible, while some may go missing, making retrieval difficult when citizens approach the civic body,” a JNAC official said.However, the civic body has not clarified how the public will access the digital records.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Torrent Pharma Q2 net profit falls 10% to Rs 534 crore despite 51% revenue growth
articles.summary: Torrent Pharma Q2 FY27 net profit falls 9.6% to Rs 534 crore despite 50.8% revenue growth to Rs 4,979 crore; EBITDA margin up to 33.5% on JB integration.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd reported a 9.6% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 534 crore for the second quarter of FY27, despite a 50.8% rise in revenue to Rs 4,979 crore.The company’s revenue growth indicated the inclusion of the JB business and stronger performance in its core markets. Operating EBITDA rose 53.8% to Rs 1,666 crore, while the operating EBITDA margin improved to 33.5% from 32.8% a year earlier.Torrent Pharma’s base business revenue grew 18% to Rs 3,893 crore, driven by branded formulations. India revenue rose 20% to Rs 2,181 crore, outpacing the Indian pharmaceutical market’s 12% growth, according to the PharmaTrac dataset cited by the company. The company reported a 32% market share for its generic semaglutide portfolio, combining oral and injectable products.Brazil revenue increased 38% to Rs 440 crore, while US revenue grew 24% to Rs 417 crore. Germany remained a weak market, with revenue declining 7% to Rs 283 crore amid supply disruptions at a third-party supplier and the loss of high-volume tenders.The JB business recorded revenue of Rs 1,086 crore during the quarter. Its integration following the merger, effective July 8, 2026, temporarily affected revenue. The company attributed the impact to integrating the India business, optimising its global business network, and aligning manufacturing and quality management systems.For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue rose 52.8% to Rs 9,900 crore. Operating EBITDA increased 57.4% to Rs 3,330 crore. Net profit declined 3.4% to Rs 1,100 crore from Rs 1,139 crore in the corresponding period last year.
